sources_considered.why: Primary experimental evidence of security harm with an older assistant; useful context for the proposed mechanism.
Controlled maintenance experiment supplies counterevidence to a blanket claim of poor code quality.
Read the research abstract. Its review-time and production-outage comparisons explicitly identify confounding; they do not establish the claimed adoption tradeoff.
Read the field-experiment paper. Completed tasks and build success do not jointly measure code volume, total review labor and vulnerabilities.
read_page returned only an author biography, so the reported findings could not be quoted or verified from its output.

evidence_items.publisher: Perry et al.; ACM CCS, author manuscript on arXiv
evidence_items.explanation: This experiment supports the possibility that AI assistance worsens security. It tested an older assistant on bounded tasks and did not measure the effect of broader adoption on total code output and review labor.

evidence_items.locator: Abstract, Results; Section 3.3.1 gives the data-collection closing date
evidence_items.explanation: The maintenance experiment found no detectable disadvantage when developers subsequently modified AI-assisted code. This weighs against a blanket quality judgment, but neither proves equivalence nor measures security and total review labor.

unresolved_gaps: The inspected evidence does not jointly identify adoption-driven output growth, total review labor and security outcomes.
Results from particular tasks and older assistants do not establish the general effect across April 2026 development workflows.
